subject: Prop 2.5 Override Supplemental Appropriations
overview: The Council implemented $7.5 million in supplemental appropriations for schools and infrastructure following the successful passage of two local override questions. It also advanced a new environmental zoning ordinance and authorized improvements to Riverside Plaza and the regional bike-share system.

items.title: Ceremonial Items and Minutes
items.summary: Tabled a resolution to congratulate the high school rowing team and the minutes of the November 12, 2024 meeting.

items.title: Green Score Zoning Amendment
items.summary: Approved a committee report and referred a proposed zoning amendment for a 'Green Score' ordinance—which creates environmental performance standards for heat and flood mitigation—to the Community Development Board.

items.title: Riverside Plaza Improvements
items.summary: Approved a $144,250 Community Preservation Act appropriation and passed the first reading of a loan order to accept a state grant for accessibility and shade improvements at Riverside Plaza. The project includes a floating deck to protect tree roots and the installation of shade sails and a water filling station.

items.title: Override Supplemental Appropriations
items.summary: Approved $7.5 million in supplemental appropriations for the Medford Public Schools and the Department of Public Works following the passage of ballot questions 7 and 8. The funding supports new teacher positions and literacy coaches as well as a dedicated road and sidewalk repair crew, while rescinding a previous $1.75 million ARPA fund advancement for the schools.

items.title: Blue Bikes Contract Authorization
items.summary: Authorized the city to enter into a future regional contract with a bike-share operator for a term exceeding three years to facilitate system growth and sponsorship.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Heard a proposal from Andrew Castagnetti to install lighting on the Cradock Bridge footbridge in memory of Larry Lepore and addressed questions regarding the upcoming meeting schedule and the Charter Commission report.
